eqn:introConstants.proof: The Dedekind zeta function $\xi$ is meromorphic near $s=1$ with a simple pole there, so $\xi'/\xi$ has a simple pole with residue $-1$ at $s=1$ and the limit defining $\mu$ exists; $\mu$ is the Euler--Kronecker constant of $E$. For $p\equiv1\pmod3$ the factor $1-2/(p(p+1))$ lies in $(0,1)$ and differs from $1$ by less than $2p^{-2}$, so the product defining $\alpha$ converges absolutely to a positive number. The terms of $\beta$ are $O(p^{-2}\log p)$, so the series converges absolutely.

thm:generalMonicCount.title: All monic cubics
thm:generalMonicCount.proof: For $f=t^3+a_1t^2+a_2t+a_3$ put $s=-a_1$ and $n(f)=a_1^2-3a_2$. Let $A_1(X)$ count the polynomials $t^3-t^2+at+b\in\ZZ[t]$ with Galois group $C_3$ and $1-3a\leq X$, and let $A_0(X)$ count the polynomials $t^3-Nt+c\in\ZZ[t]$ with Galois group $C_3$ and $1\leq N\leq X$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:generalHeightReduction}, translating the roots by an integer, and also negating them when $s\equiv-1\pmod3$, sends the polynomials of trace $s$ bijectively to those of trace $0$ (if $3\mid s$) or $1$ (if $3\nmid s$) and preserves $n(f)$, which equals $1-3a$ in trace one and $3N$ in trace zero. The same lemma shows that $H(f)\leq H$ exactly when $|s|\leq H$ and $n(f)\leq s^2+3H^2$; the bound on $a_3$ follows from the others by the arithmetic--geometric mean inequality. This gives the exact decomposition of Equation~\ref{eqn:generalTraceDecomposition}, a sum of $A_1(3H^2+s^2)$ over $3\nmid s$ and of $A_0(H^2+s^2/3)$ over $3\mid s$. Insert Equation~\ref{eqn:A1asymptotic} and Proposition~\ref{prop:traceZeroAsymptotic}, where $Q$ is the linear polynomial of Corollary~\ref{cor:integralPointCount}. The main terms become Riemann sums $\sum_{|s|\leq H,\ s\equiv r\ (\mathrm{mod}\ 3)}g(s/H)=\frac H3\int_{-1}^1g(u)\,du+O(1)$ for $g(u)=3+u^2$ and $g(u)=(3+u^2)\log(3+u^2)$, over two residue classes for $A_1$ and one for $A_0$. The two integrals in Equation~\ref{eqn:monicArchimedeanMoments} give $P$ in the form of Equation~\ref{eqn:monicConstantsFromTraceCounts}, and substituting $Q$ gives the stated $P$. Each of the $O(H)$ traces contributes an error $O_\varepsilon(H^{1+\varepsilon})$ and the Riemann-sum errors contribute $O(H^2\log H)$, so the total error is $O_\varepsilon(H^{2+\varepsilon})$.

thm:asymptoticPolynomialCount.title: Trace-one cubics
thm:asymptoticPolynomialCount.proof: Let $d_n$ be the number of $P\in(\SSS\setminus\DDD_0)(\ZZ)$ with $H(P)^2=n$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula}), and for $f=t^3-t^2+at+b$ with Galois group $C_3$ write $H_{\mathrm{tor}}(f)=\sqrt{1-3a}$, the toric height of its points (Lemma~\ref{lemma:rootVsToric}). By Equation~\ref{eqn:dSummatoryForGeneralTrace}, $\sum_{n\leq X}d_n=XQ(\tfrac12\log X)+O_\varepsilon(X^{1/2+\varepsilon})$, where $Q$ is the polynomial of Corollary~\ref{cor:integralPointCount}; the main term is the residue of $Z_0(z)X^z/z$ at the double pole $z=1$ of $Z_0(z)=\sum_{n\geq1}d_nn^{-z}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:leadingTerms}). Lemma~\ref{lemma:reducibles} removes the points of split polynomials, which are a third of the lattice points in an ellipse of area $\frac{2\pi}{3\sqrt3}X$, and halves the rest, since each polynomial with Galois group $C_3$ gives two points. This gives Equation~\ref{eqn:irrPolys}. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:rootVsToric}, $H(f)\leq H$ is equivalent to $H_{\mathrm{tor}}(f)\leq\sqrt X$ with $X=3H^2+1$. Then $\tfrac12\log X=\log H+\log\sqrt3+O(H^{-2})$, and since $Q$ is linear the main term is $\tfrac32H^2Q(\log H+\log\sqrt3)-\frac{\pi}{3\sqrt3}H^2=H^2P_1(\log H)$, with error $O_\varepsilon(H^{1+\varepsilon})$.

thm:exactFormula.title: An exact count
thm:exactFormula.proof: Let $d_n$ be the number of $P\in(\SSS\setminus\DDD_0)(\ZZ)$ with $H(P)^2=n$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula}), and let $\zeta\in E$ be a primitive cube root of unity. If $f=t^3-t^2+at+b$ has Galois group $C_3$, its roots are normal by Lemma~\ref{lemma:normalityCriterion}, since $1-3a\neq0$; so $f$ comes from an integral point of $T$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:canonicalHeight}), and Lemma~\ref{lemma:rootVsToric} gives $a\leq0$. Fix $a$ and $n=1-3a$, so that $3\nmid n$. The $d_n$ points of height $\sqrt n$ are two points for each such $f$ (Equation~\ref{eqn:polynomialWeights}) together with the split points. A split point is a triple $(x,y,z)\in\ZZ^3$ with $x+y+z=1$ and $xy+yz+zx=a$, up to cyclic permutation. Its element $\theta=x+y\zeta+z\zeta^2\in\mcO_E$ has norm $(x+y+z)^2-3(xy+yz+zx)=n$ and is congruent to $1$ modulo $1-\zeta$. Conversely, each $u+v\zeta$ with $u+v\equiv1\pmod3$ comes from exactly one triple, and a cyclic permutation multiplies $\theta$ by a power of $\zeta$. An ideal of norm $n$ has six generators $\pm\zeta^j\theta$, and exactly three of them are congruent to $1$ modulo $1-\zeta$. Hence there are $a_E(n)$ split points, and the number of polynomials is $\frac12(d_n-a_E(n))$. It remains to show $d_n=a_E(n^3)$. By Remark~\ref{rem:heightCoefficients}, $d_n$ is the product of $3k+1$ over $p^k\parallel n$ with $p\equiv1\pmod3$ if every prime $q\equiv2\pmod3$ divides $n$ to an even power, and $d_n=0$ otherwise. The ideal count $n\mapsto a_E(n^3)$ is multiplicative, so it suffices to count ideals of prime-power norm. A prime $p\equiv1\pmod3$ splits as $\mathfrak p\overline{\mathfrak p}$, and the ideals of norm $p^{3k}$ are $\mathfrak p^i\overline{\mathfrak p}^{3k-i}$ for $0\leq i\leq3k$, so there are $3k+1$ of them. A prime $q\equiv2\pmod3$ is inert with norm $q^2$, so there is one ideal of norm $q^{3k}$ if $k$ is even and none if $k$ is odd.

eqn:splitForm.context: Over $\QQ$ the surface $S$ has the equation $x_0(x_1^2+3x_2^2)=x_3^3$ (Equation~\ref{eqn:surfaceNormCubic}). Over $E$ it becomes the split form
eqn:splitForm.proof: By Proposition~\ref{prop:surfaceRationalForm}, the coordinate change of Equation~\ref{eqn:surfaceCoordinateChange} identifies $S$ with the cubic $x_0(x_1^2+3x_2^2)=x_3^3$. Over $E$ put $x_1'=x_1+\sqrt{-3}\,x_2$ and $x_2'=x_1-\sqrt{-3}\,x_2$. Then $x_1'x_2'=x_1^2+3x_2^2$, so the equation becomes $x_0x_1'x_2'=x_3^3$. The substitution is invertible, with $x_1=(x_1'+x_2')/2$ and $x_2=(x_1'-x_2')/(2\sqrt{-3})$ (Supporting lemma~\ref{helper:splittingCoordinates} with $r=\sqrt{-3}$).

eqn:surfaceQuadraticTwist.context: The split form $x_0x_1x_2=x_3^3$ (Equation~\ref{eqn:splitForm}) has the involution exchanging $x_1$ and $x_2$. For a nonsquare $d\in\QQ^\times$, its quadratic twist by $\QQ(\sqrt d)$ through this involution is
eqn:surfaceQuadraticTwist.proof: Let $r=\sqrt d\in\QQ(\sqrt d)$. Over $\QQ(\sqrt d)$ put $x_1'=x_1+rx_2$ and $x_2'=x_1-rx_2$; this substitution is invertible since $r\neq0$ (Supporting lemma~\ref{helper:splittingCoordinates}). Then $x_1'x_2'=x_1^2-dx_2^2$, so $x_0x_1'x_2'=x_3^3$ becomes $x_0(x_1^2-dx_2^2)=x_3^3$. The nontrivial automorphism $r\mapsto-r$ of $\QQ(\sqrt d)$ exchanges $x_1'$ and $x_2'$, which is the involution of the split form, and the split cubic is invariant under it. So $S^{(d)}$ is the twist of the split form by $\QQ(\sqrt d)$ through this involution. In particular $S=S^{(-3)}$.

thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula.title: The one-variable height zeta function
thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula.context: Let $\DDD_0=\{X+Y+Z=0\}\subset\SSS$. The toric height functions $H(-,s)$ of Batyrev--Tschinkel \cite{MR1369408} are indexed by $s\in\mathrm{Pic}(S)\otimes\CC$. Since $S$ has Picard rank one, we regard $s$ as a complex number, with $s=3$ corresponding to the ample generator. Then $H(-,s)=H(-)^s$, where $H(-)=H(-,1)$.
thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula.proof: Every $P\in(\SSS\setminus\DDD_0)(\ZZ)$ lies in the open torus $T$: on this affine chart $T$ is defined by $1-3e_2\neq0$, and $e_2(P)\in\ZZ$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma:affineIntegrality}. Hence the series is $Z_0(s/2)$, where $Z_0(z)=Z(2z,0,0)$ is the multivariate height zeta function $Z$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula2} on the line spanned by $D_0$; that theorem gives absolute convergence for $\operatorname{Re}(s)>2$. Lemma~\ref{lemma:simplifiedZ-s} rewrites its Euler product as $(1-3^{-z})^2\xi(z)^2R(z)$, with $R$ as in Equation~\ref{eqn:eulerCorrectionFactor}, using the Euler product of $\xi$ and the identity $(1+2x)(1-x)^2=1-3x^2+2x^3$; with $z=s/2$ this is the displayed product. The product $R(z)$ converges absolutely and locally uniformly for $\operatorname{Re}(z)>1/2$, which gives the continuation to $\operatorname{Re}(s)>1$. Since $\xi$ has only a simple pole at $1$ and $R(1)>0$, Proposition~\ref{prop:leadingTerms} shows that the only pole is a double pole at $s=2$. Finally, $S$ has Picard rank one \cite[Corollary~3.6]{odesky2023moduli}, and $-K=D_0+D_1+D_2$ is, up to torsion in the divisor class group, the ample generator \cite[Theorems~3.5 and~3.7]{odesky2023moduli}, which corresponds to $s=3$. Equation~\ref{eqn:normCharacterDivisor} shows that $3D_0$ is linearly equivalent to $-K$, so $\mathcal O(D_0)$ corresponds to $s=1$ and $H(P)$ is the toric height $H(P,\mathcal O(D_0))$.

cor:integralPointCount.title: Integral points
cor:integralPointCount.proof: Let $d_n$ be the number of $P\in(\SSS\setminus\DDD_0)(\ZZ)$ with $H(P)^2=n$. The count is $\sum_{n\leq H^2}d_n$, and by Theorem~\ref{thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula} the series $Z_0(z)=\sum_{n\geq1}d_nn^{-z}$ is the height zeta function at $s=2z$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:leadingTerms}, $Z_0$ has only a double pole at $z=1$ in $\operatorname{Re}(z)>1/2$, and its Laurent expansion there shows that the residue of $Z_0(z)X^z/z$ at $z=1$ is $XQ(\tfrac12\log X)$. Equation~\ref{eqn:dSummatoryForGeneralTrace} gives $\sum_{n\leq X}d_n=XQ(\tfrac12\log X)+O_\varepsilon(X^{1/2+\varepsilon})$. Taking $X=H^2$ gives $H^2Q(\log H)+O_\varepsilon(H^{1+2\varepsilon})$, and replacing $\varepsilon$ by $\varepsilon/2$ proves the corollary.
